submissions.findingTextShort: A 2026 critical review found inconsistent human ergogenic and recovery evidence for Cordyceps militaris across five small heterogeneous studies.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 41829950 / DOI 10.3390/nu18050781 identified five human Cordyceps militaris intervention studies totaling 321 generally young participants. Protocols varied substantially in duration, dose, training status and preparation, including multi-ingredient formulations. Selected exercise and recovery signals were reported, but the review judged the evidence inconsistent and constrained by small samples, heterogeneous protocols, incomplete randomization reporting and non-standardized products.
submissions.populationContext: Five intervention studies totaling 321 generally young participants with heterogeneous training status and exercise protocols.
submissions.usageContext: Cordyceps militaris material or multi-ingredient formulations; species and formulation identity must remain explicit.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Cordyceps militaris evidence cannot be inherited by Ophiocordyceps sinensis or generic Cordyceps products without identity matching. Multi-ingredient results cannot be attributed solely to Cordyceps. Draft-only pending registry and semantic attestation.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2026 Cordyceps militaris review describes immunomodulatory mechanisms but spans mixed evidence levels and constituent-specific effects.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 41432716 / DOI 10.1002/ptr.70144 reviews Cordyceps militaris extracts, cordycepin and polysaccharide fractions across in vitro, animal and limited clinical evidence. The mechanistic immune findings support biological plausibility and entity mapping, not a broad demonstrated human immune-efficacy claim for generic Cordyceps supplements.
submissions.usageContext: Cordyceps militaris extracts, cordycepin and polysaccharide fractions across heterogeneous evidence classes.
submissions.mechanismContext: Constituent and extract effects vary by tested immune environment; isolated-constituent evidence cannot be generalized to the whole fungus or another Cordyceps species.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The review is dominated by preclinical mechanistic evidence and includes pharmaceutical-company-affiliated authors. Clinical validation remains limited. Draft-only pending registry and semantic attestation.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2026 Cordyceps militaris polysaccharide review explicitly identifies absent clinical validation, limited pharmacokinetic data and scarce long-term safety evidence as translational bottlenecks.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 42521464 / DOI 10.1002/jsfa.70921 reviews Cordyceps militaris polysaccharides across extraction, structure-activity, functional-food, pharmacokinetic and safety domains. Despite extensive mechanistic literature, it identifies lack of clinical validation, incomplete standardization, limited digestion and pharmacokinetic data, scarce long-term safety data, and poorly characterized oral absorption, metabolism and systemic bioavailability as unresolved barriers.
submissions.usageContext: Cordyceps militaris polysaccharide fractions and functional-food translation; not generic whole-Cordyceps clinical efficacy.
submissions.safetyContext: Scarce long-term safety and exposure data are explicit evidence gaps, not proof of harm or proof of safety.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Polysaccharide composition depends on extraction, purification, molecular structure and source material. Several review authors have pharmaceutical-company affiliations. Draft-only pending registry and semantic attestation.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2026 twelve-man crossover RCT found faster post-exercise Stroop reaction time after 1 g standardized C. militaris, but no treatment-by-time interaction and no peak-VO2 benefit.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 42455764 / DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0351725 randomized 12 recreationally active young men in a double-blind crossover design to 1 g standardized Cordyceps militaris extract or placebo 30 minutes before maximal cycling. Post-exercise Stroop reaction time was faster in the Cordyceps condition, while accuracy remained near ceiling, the condition-by-time interaction was non-significant, resting oxygen uptake increased, and peak exercise VO2 did not differ. This is a small acute experimental signal, not evidence of durable cognitive enhancement or improved aerobic capacity.
submissions.populationContext: Twelve recreationally active young men in an acute randomized double-blind crossover trial.
submissions.usageContext: One gram standardized Cordyceps militaris extract taken 30 minutes before a maximal cycling test.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Very small sample, single acute exposure, selected cognitive endpoint and null peak-VO2 result prevent general exercise-performance or chronic cognition claims.

submissions.findingTextShort: A six-week randomized trial in depression with insomnia found no sleep benefit from 3 g/day C. militaris added to duloxetine; placebo improved AIS scores more.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 34858228 / DOI 10.3389/fpsyt.2021.754921 studied 59 adults with major depressive disorder and insomnia receiving duloxetine 60 mg/day plus Cordyceps militaris 3 g/day or placebo for six weeks. Athens Insomnia Scale scores and subscales decreased more in the placebo group, HAMD-17 outcomes did not differ between groups, and adverse-event incidence did not differ significantly. The result is a direct human null/counterweight for sleep efficacy and does not establish long-term or class-wide safety.
submissions.populationContext: Fifty-nine adults with major depressive disorder and insomnia in a single-center randomized double-blind placebo-controlled adjunctive trial.
submissions.usageContext: Cordyceps militaris 3 g/day for six weeks as an adjunct to duloxetine 60 mg/day; not Cordyceps monotherapy.
submissions.safetyContext: No significant adverse-event difference over six weeks does not establish rare-event, pregnancy, interaction or long-term safety.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Adjunctive duloxetine context, modest sample size, 18.6% withdrawal and six-week duration limit transfer to healthy sleepers or generic Cordyceps use.
